subject: Upton private deployment handoff — egress, DNS & routing validation
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Upton private deployment handoff — egress, DNS & routing validation

Hi Sam / Upton infra team,

Per our kickoff yesterday, we want to capture a concise preflight checklist so the infra handoff and the first-week smoke tests go smoothly. Internal owners (cc'd) will use this to validate the environment before we flip traffic to the dedicated deployment. Please confirm items you can complete on your side and call out anything that needs help from Redwood.

High-level prerequisites (ask/owner):
- VPC connectivity: VPC peering/VPN details and route table entries (Upton)
- Static egress IP(s): one or more IPs for outbound allowlisting (Upton)
- Service account with least-privilege roles + key vault/KMS access for secrets (Upton + Redwood to validate)
- DNS entries: CNAMEs and internal DNS for internal callbacks (Upton)
- Firewall rules: allow outbound ports 443, 80, 123 (NTP) and inbound for health checks as documented (Upton)
- TLS certs / trust chain or ACME access for TLS provisioning (Upton)
- Time sync and NTP reachability across hosts (Upton)
- Routing for private endpoints / internal load balancer config (Upton)

Redwood validation items (we'll perform after you confirm the above):
- Verify egress IPs from our test runs and provide sample request logs for allowlist verification
- Confirm KMS key access (we'll request a sample wrapped secret exchange)
- Run a short load test to validate connection stability and measure initial latencies

Attachments: attaching a minimal VPC template and a sample evidence bundle we typically ask for.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-template.yaml (template), upton-network-evidence.zip (evidence checklist)

Can you confirm who on the Upton side will be the point-of-contact for L3 network and who will provision the static egress IPs? If possible, share the egress IPs before the scheduled handoff.

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Customer Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Adding a couple practical validation checkpoints we'll run during the Thursday session:

1) Egress validation
- We'll execute outbound requests from the private runtime and screenshot the observed source IP to confirm it matches the two egress IPs you provision
- If outbound goes through a NAT gateway, please ensure SNAT rules preserve the static IPs for our subnet

2) KMS/Secrets exchange
- Karthik will request a wrapped secret and then attempt to unwrap it. Please confirm the service account has kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToEncrypt permissions (or equivalent)

3) Healthchecks and LB routing
- We'll hit the healthcheck endpoint and validate status codes and latency under a light load (10 rps)

4) DNS TTLs and CNAMEs
- Confirm TTLs set to values <= 60s if you plan to cut over quickly; we'll suggest temporary lower TTLs during rollouts

If you can place a short doc with the exact route table entries (subnet -> 0.0.0.0/0 via <NAT/IP>) into the Drive folder, that will speed verification.

Attachments for internal reference: network-smoke-steps.md (internal)

—Ben
